references.text: The warning not to forget the Lord after eating and becoming full, which is the direct context of the blessing after a meal.
The promise that God will provide grass in the fields so the people can eat and become full, linked to the good land.
The description of the good land flowing with milk and honey, and the call to worship the Lord for His gifts.
David's call to bless the Lord and not forget all His benefits, reflecting gratitude for God's goodness.
Thanksgiving to God who gives food to everything living, and a call to thank the God of heaven.
The promise that the people will eat and become full and praise the name of the Lord for His wonderful works.
Jesus blessed the loaves before giving them to the people, who ate and became full—a practical fulfillment of blessing God for food.
Jesus thanked God before breaking the loaves and giving them to the crowd, who ate and became full.
The one who eats, eats for the Lord and gives thanks to God, illustrating the principle of blessing God for food.
Everything God has created is good and should be received with thanksgiving, and sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
